verifications.source_context: neuroendocrine epithelia ... can be identified using known markers such as CGRP and CHGA (Figure S3A,C); human panel S3C.
verifications.reason: Paper explicitly uses CGRP as a neuroendocrine epithelial marker for identification, but CGRP is a peptide/protein name that can be encoded by CALCA or CALCB and no unique gene symbol is given; cannot be reliably normalized.

verifications.source_context: The previously published cell surface marker CD24 (Cd24a) labels prostate luminal cells, but also luminal cells of the ejaculatory ducts and urethra.
verifications.reason: Author declares CD24 labels prostate luminal cells, but it is described only as a previously published marker used to justify the choice of CD26; the authors do not use CD24 to identify/annotate prostate secretory luminal cells in this study.

verifications.source_context: We previously established PSCA as a highly specific cell surface marker capable of capturing a 94% pure population of urethral luminal cells in humans. PSCA+ urethral luminal epithelia are significantly increased in glandular BPH...
verifications.reason: PSCA is explicitly established as a cell surface marker for human urethral luminal cells and is used in this study (flow cytometry) to identify and quantify PSCA+ urethral luminal cells.

new_findings.source_context: immunofluorescent staining ... with antibodies to KRT4 (urethral luminal cells); Mouse urethral luminal cells could be identified by KRT4 staining
new_findings.reason: KRT4 is explicitly used to label and identify mouse urethral luminal cells by immunofluorescence and developmental staging.

new_findings.source_context: developed a flow cytometry scheme using Trop2 (TACSTD2) as a cell surface marker ... Trop2+ urethral luminal epithelia
new_findings.reason: Trop2/TACSTD2 is used as a cell surface marker in flow cytometry to identify and quantify mouse urethral luminal cells.

new_findings.source_context: antibodies to KRT4 (urethral luminal cells), KRT5 (basal epithelia of urethra and prostate), and NKX3.1 (secretory prostate luminal cells)
new_findings.reason: NKX3.1 is used in immunofluorescence as a marker of prostate secretory luminal cells and as a negative marker of urethral luminal cells.

new_findings.source_context: CD26 (Dpp4) which is enriched in prostate luminal epithelia over urethral luminal cells ... to specifically sort out prostate secretory luminal cells
new_findings.reason: CD26/Dpp4 is used in flow cytometry to sort and identify prostate secretory luminal cells.

new_findings.source_context: KRT13+ cells do not co-express the secretory prostate luminal marker ACPP; antibodies to ACPP (prostate secretory luminal cells)
new_findings.reason: ACPP is explicitly identified as a prostate secretory luminal cell marker and used in human immunofluorescence.

new_findings.source_context: club and hillock urethral luminal cells marked by SCGB1A1 and KRT13, respectively; KRT13 (hillock urethral cells)
new_findings.reason: KRT13 is used to mark and identify human hillock urethral luminal cells by immunofluorescence.

new_findings.source_context: club and hillock urethral luminal cells marked by SCGB1A1 and KRT13, respectively; SCGB1A1 (club urethral cells)
new_findings.reason: SCGB1A1 is used to mark and identify human club urethral luminal cells by immunofluorescence.

new_findings.cell_type: basal epithelia of urethra and prostate
new_findings.source_context: antibodies to KRT4 (urethral luminal cells), KRT5 (basal epithelia of urethra and prostate), and NKX3.1
new_findings.reason: KRT5 is used as a basal epithelial marker in mouse immunofluorescence.

new_findings.cell_type: basal epithelia of urethra and prostate
new_findings.source_context: normal human prostate labeled with antibodies to KRT13 (hillock urethral cells), KRT5 (basal cells) and ACPP (prostate secretory luminal cells)
new_findings.reason: KRT5 is used as a basal epithelial marker in human immunofluorescence.

new_findings.source_context: hierarchical flow cytometry scheme first separates leukocytes (CD45+), epithelia (CD326+), and stroma (CD45−/CD326−)
new_findings.reason: CD45 is used as a lineage marker in flow cytometry to identify and separate leukocytes.

new_findings.source_context: CD326+ epithelia are then gated into prostate secretory luminal (CD26+), basal (PDPN+) and nonbasal/nonprostate luminal (PDPN−/CD26−) cells
new_findings.reason: CD326/EPCAM is used as a lineage marker in flow cytometry to identify epithelia.

new_findings.source_context: CD326+ epithelia are then gated into prostate secretory luminal (CD26+), basal (PDPN+) and nonbasal/nonprostate luminal (PDPN−/CD26−) cells
new_findings.reason: PDPN is used as a flow cytometry marker to identify and gate basal epithelia.

issues.description: CGRP is a peptide/protein name that can be encoded by CALCA or CALCB; the paper does not provide a unique gene symbol, so the neuroendocrine marker CGRP remains unresolved.
The paper's primary cell types (urethral luminal, prostate secretory luminal, basal) are epithelial and outside L1-L4; only neuroendocrine epithelia falls in L4.
Human epithelial and BPH subcluster numbers are not explicitly reported in the Markdown; cluster inventory uses null for unspecified counts.
